I'll start by fixing the shape: the fluid is the bore cylinder (Ø40.1) minus the shaft (Ø40 with a 12×5 keyway), over the 60 mm sealed length. Building in mm first, measuring, then scaling to metres.

```python
import os, math, numpy as np, build123d as bd
print(os.getcwd(), os.listdir("."))

R_SHAFT = 20.0        # mm, 40 mm dia sealed length (given)
R_BORE  = 20.05       # mm, 40.1 mm dia bore   (given)
L       = 60.0        # mm, bore/sealed length (given)
KW_W    = 12.0        # mm keyway width        (given)
KW_D    = 5.0         # mm keyway depth        (given)
X_FLOOR = R_SHAFT - KW_D   # 15.0 mm, flat keyway floor

# keyway cutter: prism x in [15, big], |y|<=6, full length
keyway = bd.Box(30, KW_W, L, align=(bd.Align.MIN, bd.Align.CENTER, bd.Align.MIN)).moved(bd.Pos(X_FLOOR,0,0))
shaft  = bd.Cylinder(R_SHAFT, L, align=(bd.Align.CENTER,bd.Align.CENTER,bd.Align.MIN)) - keyway
bore   = bd.Cylinder(R_BORE , L, align=(bd.Align.CENTER,bd.Align.CENTER,bd.Align.MIN))
fluid  = bore - shaft
print("volume mm^3", fluid.volume, " bbox", fluid.bounding_box())
print("faces", len(fluid.faces()))
```
I'll fix the shape first: the fluid is the bore cylinder (Ø40.1) minus the shaft (Ø40 with the 12×5 keyway), over the 60 mm sealed length. Build in mm, measure, scale later.
Volume 3758.45 mm³ matches my hand calculation (377.5 gap + 3381 keyway). Now classify the 7 faces by their own geometry (surface type, radius, plane normal/offset) — not by bounding box position.

Classification is unambiguous by geometry: r=20.05 bore, r=20.0 shaft, plane x=15 floor (area 720 = 12×60 ✓), planes y=±6 flanks (244.7 = 4.079×60 ✓), two z-planes as ends. I take z=0 as the 50 mm (high-pressure) end. Now export one STL per patch, scaled to metres.
Mesher wants a manifold solid; single faces aren't. Use `export_stl` on each patch shell instead.
The cell errored only on `inspect`; re-emitting self-contained. Deflection is set in metres and tight enough (1 µm sag) that the faceted cylinders stay well inside the 50 µm clearance.
The two flanks are disjoint, so they can't sew into one shell — use a Compound.
